body:
I submit an exact rational witness for $s(90)\le 9.994038766583$, rounded upward to 12 decimal places. Its exact side is the fraction in `90/candidate.json.gz`. It is approximately 2.69816 × 10⁻¹¹ below the registered side. This supplies a feasible rational enclosure near the local solution already reported in this thread. The archived Kaggle v38 score agrees to 50 decimal places. The source map for these coordinates identifies Sargis Khachatryan and jazivxt via the Nevska compilation. The T-304 packing was credited to Joost de Winter after jazivxt. For review question 1, the reproducible description in [REGISTRATION.md](https://github.com/JoostdeWinter/square-packing/tree/3a5130340b0882e72e9d04ad2419b0437cae99aa/n90/REGISTRATION.md) is the one to retain: 44 leaning squares in T-303, 40 in the filed packing, and the positional changes described there. I have not established the origin of the earlier tiny rotation or recovered the historical LP output. The candidate stores each square as [cx, cy, t] in [0,L]², where t is the tangent of half the signed counterclockwise angle from the positive x-axis. The separate vertex checker constructs corners from those triples.

The attachment includes the input, the refined coordinates and the signed comparisons. Run `python3 -B check_vertices.py 90/candidate.json.gz` to check walls and all 4,005 pairs. The final common-center contraction makes only a precision change to the enclosed input. The comparison with the registered witness is larger. I claim feasibility; global optimality remains open.

Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology. AI tool for this certificate: GPT6.2 Astra.
